subject.title: Bug: Gateway falsely marks healthy local vLLM endpoints as timed out/overloaded, causing 1–23 min fallback cascades

question: What current-main live evidence is sufficient to choose the remaining fix for the healthy local vLLM timeout cascade?
rationale: The code shows multiple plausible timeout and routing owners, and the already-merged partial fixes make a source-only repair too likely to target the wrong layer without a fresh trace.

options.title: Require live timing trace
options.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer-owned local vLLM reproduction with provider timing, fallback, auth-profile, cron/live-session, and gateway RPC logs before queuing a repair.

options.title: Split by confirmed slice
options.body: If maintainers already know the failing layer, split the remaining issue into a narrower timeout, auth-profile, or gateway RPC item and route only that slice to repair.

options.title: Queue speculative repair
options.body: Queue a repair from source inspection alone, accepting higher risk that it changes the wrong fallback or timeout boundary.

recommendation.title: Require live timing trace
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer-owned local vLLM reproduction with provider timing, fallback, auth-profile, cron/live-session, and gateway RPC logs before queuing a repair.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is the current assignee and merged the adjacent cron fallback-preflight fix, so they are the best available routing owner for the remaining proof choice.
